item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for young people across the Commonwealth to become Wellbeing Champions for the Commonwealth Youth Council’s “Are You Okay?” Campaign, a Commonwealth-wide youth mental health and wellbeing initiative focused on starting conversations, listening to young people, strengthening connections and turning youth voices into meaningful action.

The opportunity is designed for young people who want to make a positive contribution to mental health and wellbeing within their communities. No professional mental health qualification is required. Instead, the Commonwealth Youth Council is looking for young people who care about others, are willing to listen and are committed to helping create respectful and supportive spaces where young people can speak openly about their experiences.

As a Wellbeing Champion, participants will help bring the “Are You Okay?” Campaign into their own communities. Champions are expected to encourage conversations, connect young people, amplify youth voices and contribute to a wider movement seeking to make mental health and wellbeing more visible across the Commonwealth.

The campaign itself grew out of calls made by young people at the 2024 Commonwealth Youth Forum in Samoa, where participants called for stronger action on youth mental health, including better access to services, mental health education, prevention and support. The Commonwealth Youth Council says the campaign responds by creating a Commonwealth-wide space in which young people can speak, be heard and contribute to action.

Wellbeing Champions who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact through the campaign will receive certificates of recognition. The current call closes on 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST. LinkedIn

Application deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

Official campaign page:
Commonwealth Youth Council – Are You Okay? Campaign

About the Commonwealth Youth Council

The Commonwealth Youth Council, or CYC, is the official representative voice of young people across the Commonwealth.

Established in 2013 with support from the Commonwealth Secretariat’s Commonwealth Youth Programme, the Council works to integrate young people into development processes at national, regional and Pan-Commonwealth levels.

Its work focuses particularly on:

  • Youth representation and advocacy
  • Youth empowerment and development
  • Leadership and skills development
  • Connecting youth leaders across countries
  • Creating opportunities for young people to participate meaningfully in decision-making
  • Supporting youth-led responses to shared global challenges

The Council describes itself as representing more than 1.5 billion young people and works to ensure their perspectives are included in policy and development discussions. Commonwealth Youth Council

The Wellbeing Champions opportunity forms part of that wider youth-engagement agenda.

What Is the “Are You Okay?” Campaign?

The Are You Okay? Campaign is a Commonwealth-wide youth mental health initiative built around a simple but important question:

Are you okay?

Its premise is that young people may frequently respond that they are “fine” even when they are experiencing challenges that remain unseen, unheard or unspoken.

The campaign therefore seeks to move beyond simply asking about wellbeing.

According to the Commonwealth Youth Council, it is intended to create spaces where young people can:

  • Speak about their experiences
  • Be listened to
  • Connect with others
  • Help shape meaningful action around mental health and wellbeing

The campaign is not presented simply as an awareness slogan. It attempts to connect conversations with broader youth participation and action.

Why Was the Campaign Created?

The roots of the campaign can be traced to the Commonwealth Youth Forum held in Samoa in 2024.

Young people participating in the Forum called for stronger action on youth mental health.

Among the issues raised were the need for:

  • More accessible mental health services
  • Better mental health education
  • Greater emphasis on prevention
  • Stronger support for young people’s wellbeing

The Are You Okay? Campaign was developed as a response to those calls.

Rather than treating young people simply as recipients of mental health policies, the campaign seeks to involve them directly in conversations and action.

This approach places youth voices at the centre of the initiative.

The Four Pillars of the Are You Okay? Campaign

The campaign is structured around four simple principles:

ASK — Start the conversation.

This is about taking the first step and creating opportunities for honest conversations about wellbeing.

LISTEN — Hear what young people say.

The campaign emphasizes that asking someone about their wellbeing is meaningful only when people are prepared to genuinely listen to the response.

CONNECT — Make support easier to find.

Young people may need connections to communities, networks, resources or appropriate support.

ACT — Turn voices into action.

The campaign seeks to ensure that conversations about mental health contribute to meaningful responses rather than ending with awareness alone.

The four pillars therefore move from conversation to listening, connection and action.

What Is a Wellbeing Champion?

Wellbeing Champions are young people who help bring the campaign into their own communities.

The Commonwealth Youth Council describes them as young people who take the conversation into their communities, connect peers and amplify youth voices.

This means the role is centered on community engagement and peer connection, rather than professional clinical practice.

Champions can help encourage environments in which young people feel more comfortable discussing wellbeing and recognizing that their experiences matter.

The current recruitment call particularly emphasizes three qualities:

Care, listening and commitment.

Candidates do not need to be psychologists, counselors, psychiatrists or other mental health professionals.

Instead, the programme is looking for young people who are willing to engage respectfully with others and support the broader goals of the campaign.

What Will Wellbeing Champions Do?

As a Wellbeing Champion, participants will help take the Are You Okay? Campaign from a Commonwealth-wide initiative into local communities.

The role may involve helping young people:

  • Start conversations about mental health and wellbeing
  • Feel that their experiences are heard
  • Connect with peers
  • Participate in supportive community spaces
  • Share perspectives on the issues affecting their wellbeing
  • Amplify youth voices through the campaign
  • Contribute to locally relevant campaign activities
  • Help turn conversations into broader community action

The campaign language emphasizes creating safe, respectful and supportive spaces for young people to talk, listen and connect.

The exact format of local participation may vary depending on the champion’s community and campaign activities.

You Do Not Need a Mental Health Qualification

One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that applicants do not need a professional mental health qualification.

That means the call is not limited to:

  • Psychologists
  • Medical students
  • Counselors
  • Social workers
  • Public health specialists
  • Mental health professionals

Young people from different academic, professional and community backgrounds may participate.

The Commonwealth Youth Council is explicitly looking for people who:

Care about others, can listen and want to create respectful and supportive spaces.

This makes the opportunity considerably more accessible to young people who may care strongly about wellbeing issues but have not studied psychology, medicine or a related discipline.

A Community Role, Not a Clinical Role

Applicants should nevertheless understand the nature of the position correctly.

Becoming a Wellbeing Champion does not mean becoming a therapist or mental health professional.

The campaign materials describe Champions in terms of:

  • Starting conversations
  • Listening
  • Connecting young people
  • Amplifying youth voices
  • Supporting community engagement

They do not describe Champions as providing diagnoses, therapy or clinical treatment.

This distinction is important.

The role is primarily one of youth engagement, wellbeing advocacy and supportive community connection.

Creating Spaces Where Young People Can Talk

A central idea behind the campaign is that meaningful conversations may help young people feel:

  • Seen
  • Heard
  • Connected
  • Supported

For some young people, talking openly about mental health can be difficult because of:

  • Stigma
  • Social expectations
  • Fear of judgment
  • Lack of trusted spaces
  • Limited awareness of available support

Wellbeing Champions can contribute by making conversations about wellbeing more normal and accessible in their communities.

The emphasis is not on forcing anyone to disclose personal experiences, but on helping create respectful environments where conversations can take place.

Listening as a Core Part of the Campaign

The campaign’s second pillar is LISTEN.

This matters because asking “Are you okay?” without creating space for an honest answer may have little impact.

The campaign therefore emphasizes hearing what young people actually say.

For prospective Champions, this suggests that interpersonal qualities may matter just as much as formal achievements.

Applicants who are patient, compassionate, respectful and able to listen without immediately judging others may be particularly suited to the role.

Connecting Young People

Another campaign pillar is CONNECT.

Mental health and wellbeing support can be difficult for young people to navigate.

The campaign therefore seeks to make support easier to find while building connections among young people and their communities.

Wellbeing Champions may contribute to this by strengthening peer networks and making the wider campaign visible locally.

Again, this does not mean Champions are expected to replace professional services.

Their role is community-oriented and supportive.

Turning Conversations Into Action

The fourth campaign pillar is ACT.

The initiative recognizes that awareness by itself is not necessarily enough.

Young people’s experiences can potentially inform:

  • Advocacy
  • Community activities
  • Youth programmes
  • Policy conversations
  • Future wellbeing initiatives

By participating as a Wellbeing Champion, young people have an opportunity to contribute to a larger Commonwealth conversation about what youth mental health support should look like.

The Wider Are You Okay? Campaign

Wellbeing Champions are one component of a broader campaign.

The official campaign currently includes three major elements.

The PULSE component invites young people to share their experiences anonymously, helping provide a clearer picture of youth mental health across the Commonwealth.

The Wellbeing Champions component mobilizes young people to bring conversations into their communities, connect peers and amplify youth voices.

The campaign also includes a Grand Convening scheduled for 10 October 2026, World Mental Health Day.

Together, these elements combine individual experiences, community action and wider Commonwealth engagement.

Certificates of Recognition

The programme offers an additional form of recognition for active participants.

Certificates of recognition will be awarded to Wellbeing Champions who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact through the campaign.

This is important because the certificate is connected to participation and impact rather than simply submitting an application or being named a Champion.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to engage meaningfully if selected.

What Does “Meaningful Participation” Mean?

The current public call does not provide a numerical threshold or scoring system defining meaningful participation.

Applicants should therefore not assume there is a fixed number of events or hours required unless the Commonwealth Youth Council provides additional instructions after selection.

The wording nevertheless indicates that certificates are intended to recognize Champions who actively contribute rather than simply hold the title.

Participants should therefore approach the opportunity as an active community role.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity could be particularly relevant to young people interested in areas such as youth development, wellbeing, public health, community engagement, advocacy, social development, peer support, education, communications or youth leadership.

It can also suit applicants who simply care deeply about how young people in their communities are doing.

A candidate does not need a long professional résumé.

Based on the call, some of the most relevant personal qualities are:

  • Empathy
  • Ability to listen
  • Respect for others
  • Commitment
  • Interest in youth wellbeing
  • Willingness to engage with communities
  • Desire to create supportive spaces
  • Ability to work constructively with other young people

Formal mental health credentials are explicitly not required.

Academic Qualifications

The current Wellbeing Champion call does not specify a mandatory degree or academic qualification.

Applicants are not told that they must:

  • Be university students
  • Hold a Bachelor’s degree
  • Hold a Master’s degree
  • Study psychology
  • Study medicine
  • Study public health

The central qualification described in the call is commitment to supporting young people and participating responsibly in the campaign.

This makes the opportunity potentially accessible to young people with a wide variety of educational backgrounds.

Professional Experience

No minimum number of years of employment or professional experience is stated.

The call does not require previous employment in:

  • Healthcare
  • Mental health
  • NGOs
  • Community development
  • Youth organizations

Previous volunteering, peer support or community-engagement experience may naturally be relevant, but the published call does not make such experience mandatory.

Is This Opportunity Open Internationally?

The opportunity is framed specifically around young people across the Commonwealth.

The Commonwealth currently consists of 56 independent member countries across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and Americas, Europe and the Pacific.

The call does not provide a separate country-by-country eligibility rule distinguishing citizenship from residence.

Applicants should therefore understand the geographic target as the Commonwealth community, rather than assume it is a completely unrestricted global programme.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

Candidates in different time zones should pay attention to the use of British Summer Time rather than assuming the deadline refers to their local midnight.

Because this is a time-specific deadline, applicants are encouraged to submit before the final hours.

Key Information at a Glance

  • Programme: Are You Okay? Wellbeing Champions
  • Organizer: Commonwealth Youth Council
  • Focus: Youth mental health and wellbeing
  • Geographic focus: Commonwealth countries
  • Role: Community-based youth wellbeing champion
  • Professional mental health qualification: Not required
  • Main activities: Starting conversations, listening, connecting peers, amplifying youth voices and supporting community action
  • Recognition: Certificates for Champions demonstrating meaningful participation and impact
  • Campaign pillars: Ask, Listen, Connect and Act
  • Grand Convening: 10 October 2026, World Mental Health Day
  • Application deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST
  • Official campaign page: https://cycofficial.org/are-you-okay/
  • Application: https://lnkd.in/e5ttrdqQ

Why This Opportunity Matter

Mental health discussions are often framed around professional services, but supportive communities can also play an important role in whether young people feel comfortable speaking about the difficulties they face.

The Are You Okay? Campaign takes a youth-led approach by involving young people directly in starting conversations and identifying what support and action may be needed.

That approach also reflects the broader role of the Commonwealth Youth Council, which works to increase meaningful youth participation rather than simply discussing young people without involving them.

For participants, becoming a Wellbeing Champion offers an opportunity to contribute to a Commonwealth-wide initiative while bringing its goals into a local community.

It may also help young people develop transferable experience in:

  • Youth engagement
  • Advocacy
  • Community mobilization
  • Communication
  • Listening
  • Wellbeing promotion
  • Leadership
  • Peer engagement

However, the most important element of the programme remains its central purpose: helping create communities where young people feel able to speak and know that someone is willing to listen.

Conclusion

The Commonwealth Youth Council Are You Okay? Wellbeing Champions 2026 opportunity invites young people across the Commonwealth to play an active role in strengthening conversations around youth mental health and wellbeing.

The campaign is built around four straightforward principles — Ask, Listen, Connect and Act — and responds to calls made by young people at the 2024 Commonwealth Youth Forum for stronger action on mental health.

Applicants do not need professional mental health qualifications. Instead, the Council is seeking young people who care about others, can listen respectfully and are committed to creating supportive spaces within their communities.

Selected Champions will help bring the campaign into their communities, connect young people and amplify youth voices. Those who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact can receive certificates of recognition.

For a young person interested in wellbeing, youth advocacy, community engagement or simply helping create spaces where people feel more comfortable talking about how they are doing, this is an accessible opportunity to participate in a wider Commonwealth movement.

Applications close on 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST.

Deadline: October 13, 2026

IREX is seeking academic, professional, and regional experts to serve as application readers for the 2027 Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders.

About the Mandela Washington Fellowship

The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the flagship exchange program of the Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI).

In summer 2027, the Fellowship will bring up to 550 accomplished young African leaders to the United States for a comprehensive, executive-style program designed to strengthen leadership skills, build professional networks, and support collaboration between African and American counterparts.

Fellows participate in academic coursework, professional site visits, and structured networking activities. The program focuses on strengthening collaboration in areas including U.S.-Africa trade and economic prosperity, technological innovation, and peace and security.

The Mandela Washington Fellowship is a program of the U.S. Department of State, funded by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX.

Call for Application Readers

IREX is looking for individuals who can review and score applications using established guidelines and a structured scoring rubric.

Over the past twelve years, application readers have helped assess nearly 478,000 applications from 49 sub-Saharan African countries for approximately 7,800 Fellowship places.

Serving as an application reader provides an opportunity to contribute to a fair and merit-based selection process while gaining insight into emerging priorities, challenges, and locally driven solutions across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Readers may also gain valuable exposure to fellowship selection practices, promising African leaders, and key issues affecting the continent.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suited to academics, professionals, and regional experts with expertise in one or more of the Fellowship’s thematic areas:

  • Business and trade
  • Emerging technologies
  • Governance and security

Experience working in Africa or on sub-Saharan African issues is also relevant.

While expertise in these areas is ideal, it is not a requirement to serve as a reader.

Reader Honorarium

Eligible readers may opt to receive a one-time $100 honorarium for their service.

However:

  • U.S. Government employees and contractors are not eligible to receive the honorarium.
  • IREX cannot make international wire payments.
  • Readers receiving the honorarium must have a U.S. bank account in their own name capable of receiving an ACH/direct deposit transfer.
  • Eligible readers who choose to receive the honorarium must submit a completed W-9 form to IREX for tax purposes.

Application Deadline and Reading Period

Interested individuals should complete the 2027 Reader Application by:

📅 October 13, 2026

The application reading period is expected to begin in mid-October 2026 and continue through mid-November 2026. Selected readers will be contacted by IREX in October.

How to Apply

To support the selection of the next cohort of Mandela Washington Fellows, complete the Reader Application before the October 13, 2026 deadline.

Please feel free to share this opportunity with qualified colleagues and professional networks.

Questions?

For questions about becoming an application reader, contact:

MWFReaders@irex.org

 

Interested professionals are invited to complete the Reader Application by October 13, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
EvalYouth Asia (EYA) has opened applications for its 2026 Core Group, inviting passionate young and emerging evaluators to take an active leadership role in strengthening evaluation practice, youth leadership, networking, and collaboration across the Asia-Pacific region.

This is a volunteer leadership opportunity for individuals who are passionate about evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making and who want to contribute to a regional network supporting the next generation of evaluation professionals.

Selected Core Group members will have the opportunity to contribute to strategic planning, develop initiatives for young and emerging evaluators, strengthen national and regional networks, build partnerships, and help shape the future direction of EvalYouth Asia.

About EvalYouth Asia

EvalYouth Asia is a regional platform that works to strengthen the participation and leadership of young and emerging evaluators (YEEs) within the evaluation community across Asia and the Pacific.

Established in 2019, EvalYouth Asia has focused on creating opportunities for young and emerging evaluators to connect with one another, develop their professional capacities, exchange knowledge, and participate meaningfully in the wider evaluation community.

The network is driven by volunteers who contribute their time, expertise, and ideas to create a stronger and more connected community of emerging evaluation professionals.

Through its activities, EvalYouth Asia seeks to provide young evaluators with opportunities to:

  • Build professional networks across the Asia-Pacific region.
  • Exchange knowledge and experiences in evaluation.
  • Develop their leadership and professional skills.
  • Participate in regional and global evaluation discussions.
  • Engage with evaluation associations and other professional organizations.
  • Strengthen youth participation in the evaluation field.
  • Contribute to the development of the next generation of evaluation leaders.

For 2026, EvalYouth Asia is seeking new Core Group members who can contribute their skills, perspectives, leadership, and commitment to the continued development of the regional network.

What Is the EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group?

The Core Group is a volunteer leadership group responsible for helping guide and implement the activities of EvalYouth Asia.

Joining the Core Group is more than simply becoming a member of a professional network. Successful applicants will be expected to actively participate in planning, decision-making, community engagement, partnerships, and the development of initiatives benefiting young and emerging evaluators across the region.

Core Group members will work collaboratively with other volunteers and regional partners to help strengthen the evaluation community and create opportunities for young professionals.

Key Responsibilities of Core Group Members

Selected members will contribute to a range of strategic, programmatic, networking, and community-building activities.

1. Provide Strategic Leadership

Core Group members will help provide strategic leadership for the EvalYouth Asia network.

This includes contributing ideas, participating in discussions about the network’s direction, and helping identify activities and initiatives that can strengthen opportunities for young and emerging evaluators throughout the Asia-Pacific region.

Members will therefore have an opportunity to contribute not only to individual activities but also to the broader development and direction of the regional network.

2. Design and Implement Regional Initiatives

Core Group members will help design and implement initiatives that support young and emerging evaluators.

These initiatives may contribute to areas such as:

  • Professional development.
  • Capacity building.
  • Knowledge exchange.
  • Networking.
  • Youth leadership.
  • Engagement within the evaluation community.
  • Collaboration between young evaluators and established evaluation organizations.

Members will be able to contribute their own ideas and expertise while working collaboratively with other members of the Core Group.

3. Strengthen National and Regional EvalYouth Networks

Another important responsibility will be supporting the development and strengthening of EvalYouth networks at both the national and regional levels.

Core Group members will work to encourage collaboration among existing networks and support efforts to establish new country chapters where appropriate.

This provides an opportunity for individuals interested in regional network development and youth-led professional communities to contribute to a broader evaluation movement.

4. Build Partnerships With Key Stakeholders

Core Group members will also contribute to partnership-building efforts.

They will work to establish and strengthen relationships with:

  • Evaluation associations.
  • Development organizations.
  • Professional evaluation networks.
  • Other relevant stakeholders.
  • Regional and international partners.

The objective is to expand opportunities for youth engagement and create stronger connections between young and emerging evaluators and the wider evaluation ecosystem.

5. Collaborate With Regional Evaluation Organizations

The Core Group will work closely with organizations and networks involved in evaluation across the region.

This includes collaboration with the Asia Pacific Evaluation Association (APEA), Voluntary Organizations for Professional Evaluation (VOPEs), and other regional partners.

Such collaboration can help create stronger links between young and emerging evaluators and established evaluation institutions and professional networks.

6. Participate in Monthly Core Group Meetings

Core Group members are expected to participate in monthly Core Group meetings.

These meetings provide an important space for members to:

  • Discuss ongoing activities.
  • Plan future initiatives.
  • Make decisions.
  • Coordinate responsibilities.
  • Share updates.
  • Discuss challenges and opportunities.
  • Contribute ideas for strengthening the network.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to maintain an ongoing commitment throughout their term.

7. Engage With EvalYouth Asia Members

Core Group members will also be expected to regularly engage with the wider EvalYouth Asia community.

This includes supporting community-building activities and helping maintain an active, connected, and collaborative network of young and emerging evaluators across the region.

Community engagement is an important part of the role because the Core Group’s activities are intended to respond to the needs and interests of the wider EvalYouth Asia membership.

Volunteer Commitment

The EvalYouth Asia Core Group is a voluntary leadership opportunity.

Selected members are expected to dedicate approximately 20 hours per month to Core Group responsibilities.

This means applicants should carefully consider whether they have sufficient time and availability to make a meaningful contribution alongside their existing academic, professional, or other commitments.

In addition to the regular monthly commitment, each Core Group member is expected to lead or co-lead at least one major EvalYouth Asia initiative or workstream during their term.

This requirement emphasizes the active leadership component of the opportunity.

Applicants should therefore be prepared not only to attend meetings but also to take responsibility for delivering a substantial initiative or area of work.

Who Should Apply?

EvalYouth Asia is looking for young and emerging evaluators across the Asia-Pacific region who are interested in contributing to the development of evaluation practice and youth leadership.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to individuals who demonstrate the following qualities:

Passion for Evaluation

Applicants should have a genuine interest in evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making.

An interest in understanding what works, generating and using evidence, improving programs, and supporting better decision-making can be particularly relevant to the role.

Commitment to the Evaluation Community

Applicants should be committed to strengthening the evaluation community within the Asia-Pacific region.

This includes an interest in supporting other young and emerging evaluators and contributing to a stronger regional evaluation ecosystem.

Collaborative Approach

Core Group work involves collaboration with other volunteers, evaluation organizations, development organizations, and regional and international partners.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable working with others and contributing constructively to collaborative initiatives.

Proactive and Willing to Contribute

The role requires active participation rather than passive membership.

Applicants should be willing to contribute their:

  • Time.
  • Skills.
  • Knowledge.
  • Ideas.
  • Professional experience.
  • Leadership.

The expected commitment of approximately 20 hours per month makes availability and willingness to contribute important considerations.

Interest in Regional and International Collaboration

Applicants should be interested in working with diverse partners across the Asia-Pacific region and potentially engaging with regional and international organizations connected to evaluation and development.

Why Join the EvalYouth Asia Core Group?

Becoming part of the Core Group can provide an opportunity to contribute to the development of a regional professional community while gaining practical experience in leadership, collaboration, networking, and initiative management.

Key areas of potential professional development include:

Regional Networking

Members can engage with young and emerging evaluators and evaluation stakeholders across the Asia-Pacific region.

Leadership Experience

Core Group members will participate in strategic decision-making and are expected to lead or co-lead a major initiative or workstream.

Program and Initiative Development

Members can gain practical experience in designing and implementing activities intended to support young evaluators.

Partnership Building

Working with evaluation associations, development organizations, VOPEs, APEA, and other partners can provide exposure to regional professional networks.

Knowledge Exchange

The network provides a platform for sharing ideas, experiences, and knowledge related to evaluation.

Youth Leadership in Evaluation

The Core Group provides an avenue for young and emerging evaluators to contribute directly to the development of the evaluation community and strengthen youth leadership within the field.

Geographic Scope of the Opportunity

The Core Group opportunity is intended for young and emerging evaluators across the Asia-Pacific region.

The announcement does not provide a specific list of eligible countries. Therefore, applicants should interpret the geographic eligibility according to EvalYouth Asia’s definition and scope of the Asia-Pacific region and confirm any country-specific requirements through the official application information.

There is also no race, ethnicity, or racial-group restriction stated in the announcement.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group is:

October 1, 2026

Applicants should ensure that they submit their applications before the stated deadline.

Because the announcement provides the deadline only as October 1 and does not specify a particular time or time zone, applicants should check the official application instructions for the exact submission time and any additional requirements.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should carefully consider how their experience, interests, and skills align with the responsibilities of a Core Group member.

When preparing an application, it can be useful to demonstrate:

  1. Your interest in evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making.
  2. Your experience or involvement in evaluation, where applicable.
  3. Your interest in youth leadership and professional community development.
  4. Your ability to collaborate with people from different backgrounds and organizations.
  5. Your availability to contribute approximately 20 hours per month.
  6. Your leadership potential, particularly examples of initiatives, projects, or activities you have helped organize or lead.
  7. Your interest in regional collaboration across the Asia-Pacific region.
  8. Your ideas for supporting young and emerging evaluators and strengthening the EvalYouth Asia network.

Applicants should also consider which skills they could contribute to the Core Group, whether in research, evaluation, communications, partnerships, project management, community engagement, training, networking, or another relevant area.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group is a volunteer leadership opportunity for young and emerging evaluators interested in strengthening evaluation practice, youth leadership, networking, and collaboration across the Asia-Pacific region.

Since its establishment in 2019, EvalYouth Asia has worked to create opportunities for young and emerging evaluators to connect, develop their capacities, exchange knowledge, and participate meaningfully in the evaluation community. The 2026 Core Group will continue this work by bringing together committed volunteers who can provide leadership, develop initiatives, strengthen national and regional networks, build partnerships, and engage with members.

Selected members will be expected to dedicate approximately 20 hours per month and lead or co-lead at least one major initiative or workstream during their term.

Young and emerging evaluators across the Asia-Pacific region who are passionate about evaluation, evidence-informed decision-making, collaboration, and regional professional development are encouraged to consider applying.

Application Deadline: October 1, 2026

item.content:encoded:
The AFS Youth Assembly is inviting its alumni to apply to become Impact Coordinators, a significant global leadership opportunity designed for young changemakers who want to help transform ideas into measurable social impact while strengthening youth-led initiatives across different regions of the world.

Launched as part of the next phase of the AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network, the Impact Coordinator opportunity places selected alumni at the center of regional youth engagement, project development, mentorship, collaboration, and impact-building. Impact Coordinators will serve for a two-year term, working with Youth Assembly alumni in their respective regions and helping them develop ideas, identify resources, connect with relevant opportunities, and advance projects that contribute to positive social change.

A particularly attractive benefit of the opportunity is that selected Impact Coordinators will receive a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, Switzerland. Coordinators will also receive training support and an AFS Global Competence Certificate while developing practical leadership, communication, organizational, mentoring, networking, and project coordination skills.

About the AFS Youth Assembly

The AFS Youth Assembly is an international platform that brings together young leaders, changemakers, social entrepreneurs, activists, students, professionals, educators, and other individuals committed to building more inclusive, peaceful, sustainable, and equitable societies.

The platform focuses on helping emerging leaders connect across borders, develop global competence, acquire practical skills, build partnerships, and translate ideas into action.

The Youth Assembly was founded in 2004 by the Friendship Ambassadors Foundation and is now part of AFS Intercultural Programs. AFS is an international nonprofit organization focused on intercultural learning and the development of knowledge, skills, and understanding that can contribute to a more just and peaceful world.

The Youth Assembly is intended to be more than a stand-alone international gathering. Participants are encouraged to continue their development and community engagement after attending the Assembly through opportunities such as the Alumni Impact Network, leadership roles, mentoring, project development, collaboration, and other AFS activities.

What Is the AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network?

The AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network is a global community created to help former Youth Assembly participants continue developing their ideas and generating impact after the Assembly.

Rather than allowing the Youth Assembly experience to end when delegates return home, the network provides a structure through which alumni can remain connected, collaborate with other changemakers, obtain mentorship, access useful resources, develop their skills, pursue project support, and showcase their achievements.

The network is designed to support alumni in several important areas, including:

  • Developing and implementing action-oriented projects;
  • Receiving mentorship and connections to relevant experts;
  • Accessing opportunities for seed funding;
  • Building regional and international partnerships;
  • Connecting with other Youth Assembly alumni;
  • Showcasing successful projects and achievements internationally;
  • Participating in skills-development activities; and
  • Receiving peer-to-peer support from other young changemakers.

The Alumni Impact Network is open to people who have previously participated in a session of the Youth Assembly.

Why AFS Is Recruiting Impact Coordinators

Following the 31st AFS Youth Assembly held in Geneva in August 2026, the Alumni Impact Network is moving into another stage of its development.

AFS is coordinating alumni engagement and impact activities across six major geographic regions:

  1. Africa
  2. Asia and Oceania
  3. Europe
  4. Latin America and the Caribbean
  5. Middle East and North Africa
  6. North America

Impact Coordinators are intended to provide the regional leadership needed to connect alumni, encourage collaboration and help turn promising ideas into practical initiatives.

They will effectively serve as an important connection between the wider AFS Youth Assembly network and alumni working on projects and initiatives within their regions.

What Does an AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Do?

An Impact Coordinator is expected to be more than a representative or titleholder. The position involves actively engaging with Youth Assembly alumni and helping create an environment where ideas, partnerships, resources, mentorship, and youth-led action can come together.

Coordinators will help alumni progress from having an idea to developing and implementing meaningful activities.

Their work can involve motivating alumni, connecting changemakers with one another, identifying useful resources, helping projects gain visibility and keeping AFS informed about the progress being made within their region.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to applicants who already have practical experience in youth engagement, social entrepreneurship, community projects, mentoring, sustainable development, advocacy, nonprofit activities or other forms of social impact.

Key Responsibilities of an Impact Coordinator

Selected Impact Coordinators will take on several major responsibilities during their two-year leadership term.

1. Provide Regional Leadership

Impact Coordinators will help organize and mobilize Youth Assembly alumni within the region they represent.

This requires maintaining engagement among alumni rather than simply communicating with them occasionally. Coordinators should be capable of encouraging participation, building relationships and creating a stronger regional community of changemakers.

2. Organize Alumni Engagement Activities

Coordinators are expected to bring alumni together through regular engagement.

Depending on circumstances, this may include:

  • Virtual meetings;
  • In-person gatherings;
  • Networking activities;
  • Collaborative discussions;
  • Project-focused sessions; and
  • Other opportunities that encourage alumni to work together.

The broader purpose is to create meaningful collaboration rather than allowing alumni projects to operate entirely in isolation.

3. Help Alumni Turn Ideas into Action

An important part of the position involves supporting alumni who have ideas for social-impact projects or initiatives.

Impact Coordinators should understand how ideas can be developed into practical projects and should be able to help other young changemakers move through this process.

This is one reason AFS is specifically looking for candidates who understand project ideation and who have previously started or participated in successful projects, initiatives or social ventures.

4. Provide Mentorship and Support

Impact Coordinators will have an important mentoring function.

They will help Youth Assembly alumni navigate the challenges involved in developing projects and generating social impact. Candidates with previous mentoring experience or experience working directly with young people are therefore particularly relevant to the role.

5. Connect Alumni with Resources

Successful social-impact initiatives often require more than a good idea. They may require partnerships, mentorship, technical knowledge, networks, visibility or financial resources.

Impact Coordinators are therefore expected to understand the youth and social-impact ecosystem and have knowledge of useful resources such as:

  • Impact hubs;
  • Youth networks;
  • Potential partners;
  • Mentors;
  • Relevant organizations;
  • Project-development resources; and
  • Other opportunities that could assist alumni.

The wider Alumni Impact Network itself is designed to connect participants with support mechanisms that include mentorship, expert connections and opportunities for seed funding.

6. Encourage Collaboration

Another major responsibility will be connecting Youth Assembly alumni with one another.

Instead of individual changemakers working separately on similar problems, the network aims to encourage cooperation, knowledge sharing and partnerships.

Strong coordinators should therefore be comfortable bringing people together, facilitating communication and encouraging collaborative action.

7. Track Projects and Progress

Impact Coordinators will also help monitor the progress of projects being implemented or supported within their regions.

They will communicate relevant updates to AFS staff, helping the organization understand how alumni projects and initiatives are progressing.

For candidates interested in international development, project management, monitoring, community engagement or nonprofit leadership, this responsibility provides particularly useful practical experience.

8. Promote Alumni Projects Globally

Successful initiatives should not remain invisible.

Impact Coordinators will help showcase the projects and achievements of Youth Assembly alumni to a wider international audience.

This can increase recognition for youth-led initiatives while allowing successful ideas, experiences and lessons to reach other members of the international AFS community.

Benefits of Becoming an AFS Impact Coordinator

Although the Impact Coordinator position is a volunteer role, it comes with substantial professional-development, leadership and networking benefits.

Full Scholarship to the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva

One of the most significant benefits is a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, Switzerland.

This gives selected coordinators the opportunity to return to the international Youth Assembly environment while continuing their leadership journey within the AFS community.

Two Years of Global Leadership Experience

Selected candidates will serve as Impact Coordinators for two years.

A two-year term provides considerably more opportunity to build meaningful relationships, support projects and demonstrate sustained leadership than a short-term volunteer assignment.

International Recognition

Impact Coordinators and the projects they facilitate may be highlighted through social networks and other AFS visibility channels.

This can help coordinators demonstrate their contributions to social impact while increasing the visibility of the initiatives they support.

Leadership and Professional Skills Development

The position provides opportunities to practice skills that can be valuable in future academic and professional settings, including:

  • Leadership;
  • Project coordination;
  • Mentoring;
  • Community building;
  • Stakeholder engagement;
  • Communication;
  • Networking;
  • Organization;
  • Teamwork;
  • Independent working;
  • Project monitoring; and
  • Social-impact development.

AFS Global Competence Certificate

Impact Coordinators will receive an AFS Global Competence Certificate, together with additional training support.

The experience can therefore provide both practical leadership exposure and structured professional development.

Access to a Global Changemaker Community

Impact Coordinators will operate within an established international community of Youth Assembly alumni and changemakers.

The Alumni Impact Network exists specifically to encourage regional and international collaboration, mentorship, project development, access to resources and opportunities for alumni to increase their impact.

Eligibility Requirements for the Impact Coordinator Opportunity

Applicants should review the requirements carefully because this opportunity is not open to the general public.

The most important eligibility requirement is previous participation in the AFS Youth Assembly.

Previous AFS Youth Assembly Participation Is Mandatory

Applicants must have previously attended the AFS Youth Assembly.

AFS explicitly states that the Impact Coordinator position is open only to Youth Assembly alumni. Therefore, someone with excellent leadership or social-impact experience who has never attended the Youth Assembly would not satisfy this fundamental requirement.

Applicants Must Live in the Region They Want to Represent

Candidates must currently live in the geographic region for which they want to serve as an Impact Coordinator.

The six regions covered by the initiative are Africa, Asia and Oceania, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, Middle East and North Africa, and North America.

Strong Interest in Social Impact and the SDGs

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine commitment to social impact and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This is central to the wider mission of the Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network, which seeks to translate youth leadership into practical action addressing social, environmental and development challenges.

Experience Working with Young People

AFS is seeking applicants with experience working with youth.

Relevant experience could include areas such as mentoring young people or participating in the creation and implementation of action-oriented projects.

Project or Social Venture Experience

Applicants should have started or participated in a successful:

  • Project;
  • Initiative; or
  • Social venture.

This requirement reflects the practical nature of the coordinator role. Candidates will be helping other alumni develop their own initiatives, making previous firsthand project experience particularly valuable.

Understanding of Project Ideation

Candidates should have strong knowledge of the ideation process and understand how social projects and ventures are developed.

This can help coordinators guide alumni from identifying a problem or opportunity through to shaping and advancing a workable initiative.

Networks and Knowledge of Resources

Applicants should have useful connections or knowledge of resources relevant to social-impact work.

These may include impact hubs, organizations, youth resources, partners and other networks that could help Youth Assembly alumni move their projects forward.

Leadership and Communication Skills

AFS is looking for candidates who can demonstrate strong:

  • Leadership skills;
  • Communication skills;
  • Coordination skills; and
  • Organizational abilities.

These competencies are particularly important because coordinators will be responsible for bringing together people from different backgrounds and supporting multiple activities and initiatives.

Ability to Work Independently and Collaboratively

Candidates should be capable of managing responsibilities independently while also working effectively as part of a wider international network.

Computer and Internet Access

Applicants must have personal access to:

  • A computer; and
  • Stable internet connectivity.

This is particularly important because regional and international coordination may involve substantial online communication and virtual engagement.

Time Commitment

Applicants must be willing and able to dedicate sufficient time and effort to the role throughout the appointment.

Potential candidates should therefore consider whether they can realistically maintain an active leadership commitment alongside their academic, professional and personal responsibilities.

English Language Proficiency

Candidates must be proficient in written and spoken English.

Because the position operates within an international network, effective English communication is an important requirement.

Social Media Skills

Applicants should also be comfortable using social media and digital tools for communication and networking.

This aligns with the coordinator’s responsibility to connect alumni and help promote youth-led projects and achievements.

Connection to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals

The Impact Coordinator initiative has a strong relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals.

The AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network is built around supporting youth-led action on major global and regional challenges. The Declaration of Impact 2026, launched during the 31st AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, establishes shared global and regional priorities and emphasizes collaboration, inclusion, education, equality, sustainability, innovation, health and well-being, and youth leadership.

Impact Coordinators can therefore play an important role in helping young changemakers translate broad sustainable-development ambitions into practical regional and community-level initiatives.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for eligible Youth Assembly alumni who see themselves as facilitators and community builders rather than individuals interested only in adding another title to their résumé.

Strong potential applicants are likely to be people who enjoy:

  • Helping other young leaders succeed;
  • Mentoring and advising peers;
  • Developing social-impact projects;
  • Building partnerships;
  • Organizing communities and networks;
  • Connecting people with resources;
  • Promoting youth-led initiatives;
  • Working toward the Sustainable Development Goals;
  • Communicating across cultures; and
  • Taking responsibility for long-term initiatives.

Applicants should also be prepared for the reality that this is an active two-year volunteer commitment rather than a passive honorary position.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the official AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator announcement.

Because the official announcement provides an application link without publishing a closing date, interested and eligible Youth Assembly alumni should check the current application status and consider submitting their application as early as possible rather than assuming that applications will remain open indefinitely.

How to Apply for the AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Opportunity

Eligible applicants should complete the official Impact Coordinator application provided by the AFS Youth Assembly.

Before applying, candidates should ensure that they:

  1. Have previously participated in the AFS Youth Assembly;
  2. Currently live in the region they intend to represent;
  3. Can demonstrate youth engagement or mentoring experience;
  4. Have relevant experience with projects, initiatives or social ventures;
  5. Understand social-project development and ideation;
  6. Can demonstrate leadership, communication, coordination and organizational abilities;
  7. Have sufficient time to commit to the two-year role;
  8. Have reliable access to a computer and stable internet;
  9. Are proficient in spoken and written English; and
  10. Are comfortable using social media and online networking tools.

Official AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Announcement and Application

Why This Opportunity Matters

The AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator opportunity provides alumni with a chance to move from participating in an international youth platform to helping shape what happens after delegates return to their communities.

The role is particularly significant because it focuses on the stage where many promising youth initiatives face their greatest challenge: converting enthusiasm and ideas into sustained action.

By connecting alumni with mentorship, resources, partnerships, collaboration and wider visibility, Impact Coordinators can help create stronger regional ecosystems for youth-led change.

For the coordinators themselves, the opportunity combines practical leadership experience, international networking, skills development, global recognition, training support and a full scholarship to attend the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva.

Conclusion

The AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator 2026 opportunity is an attractive international leadership opportunity for Youth Assembly alumni who have demonstrated commitment to youth empowerment, social impact and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Selected coordinators will undertake a two-year volunteer leadership role, helping organize and motivate alumni, support youth-led projects, connect changemakers with useful resources, encourage collaboration, monitor project progress and increase the global visibility of alumni initiatives.

In return, coordinators can gain significant leadership and professional-development experience, receive training support and an AFS Global Competence Certificate, strengthen their international networks, gain recognition for their contributions and receive a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva.

However, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the principal eligibility condition: only previous Youth Assembly participants are eligible to become Impact Coordinators.

Anthropic is inviting undergraduate, graduate, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers to apply for its Claude Campus Ambassador Program. Selected ambassadors will receive a USD 3,600 cash stipend while leading AI-focused activities, workshops, discussions and research events on campus.

Key Details

  • Host organisation: Anthropic
  • Opportunity: Claude Campus Ambassador Program
  • Who can apply: Undergraduate students, graduate students, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers
  • Benefits: USD 3,600 cash stipend
  • Focus areas: Artificial intelligence, AI building, education, research and science
  • Programme tracks: Claude Builder Club, Claude Campus Conversations and Claude for Science
  • Application deadline: September 12 at 11:59pm PT
  • Location: University campuses / student communities worldwide
  • Apply: Apply Now

Supporting Student Builders

Lead Student-Driven AI Initiatives with Support from Anthropic

The Claude Campus Ambassador Program is back, with applications open for builders, thinkers and researchers.

The programme provides students with an opportunity to bring AI fluency to their campuses, connect with other students interested in artificial intelligence, organise events and workshops, and engage with Anthropic teams.

The programme has three tracks depending on your level of study and interests.

Undergraduate Students – Claude Builder Club

Build Something Real

If you’re passionate about bringing AI fluency to your campus, apply to lead a Claude Builder Club.

As a Claude Builder Club ambassador, you will:

  • Collaborate with Anthropic to establish and lead a club for AI builders on your campus
  • Organise technical and non-technical workshops featuring Anthropic guest speakers
  • Run hackathons and demo nights for student builders
  • Share regular updates, tips and resources, including API credits, with members
  • Receive a USD 3,600 cash stipend

The official programme materials describe this track as an opportunity to lead a Claude Builder Club, organise workshops, run hackathons and share API credits with other members.

Graduate Students – Claude Campus Conversations

Lead the Conversation

If you’re a STEM or humanities master’s student passionate about ensuring AI has a positive impact on education and society, you can apply to lead Claude Campus Conversations.

You will:

  • Host discussion groups and events with fellow students on the big questions in AI and society
  • Help students build AI fluency by creating spaces to showcase and discuss their Claude builds
  • Visit the Anthropic office and connect with the global ambassador community
  • Receive a USD 3,600 cash stipend

The programme focuses on creating spaces where students can discuss important questions around AI and share their work and builds.

PhD Students & Postdoctoral Researchers – Claude for Science

Take Your Research Further

If you’re a PhD student or postdoctoral researcher using AI to advance research, apply to lead Claude for Science workshops for fellow researchers.

You will:

  • Lead a community of AI-native PhD scientists and postdocs on your campus
  • Organise Claude for Science workshops
  • Join speaker events with Anthropic’s math and science teams
  • Build your expertise on how AI is changing science fields
  • Engage with Anthropic scientists through workshops and research
  • Receive a USD 3,600 cash stipend

The programme materials specifically highlight Claude for Science workshops, speaker events and engagement with Anthropic’s math and science teams on student programming and research.

Why Become a Claude Campus Ambassador?

Joining the programme gives students the opportunity to develop their AI knowledge while building communities and connecting with Anthropic.

Access AI Workshops Led by Anthropic

Gain AI skills while collaborating with Anthropic’s teams to bring AI fluency to your campus.

Find Your People

Connect with students from around the world who see the potential for AI to expand human flourishing.

Help Shape the Future of Claude

Engage with Anthropic teams on Claude features and product ideas. Your feedback can influence Claude’s development.

How Much Does the Claude Campus Ambassador Program Pay?

Selected ambassadors receive a USD 3,600 cash stipend.

This makes the Claude Campus Ambassador Program a paid student opportunity for undergraduate students, graduate students, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers participating in the relevant programme tracks.

Claude Campus Ambassador Application Deadline

Applications close at 11:59pm PT on September 12.

If you are interested in becoming a Claude Campus Ambassador, apply before the deadline.

👉 Apply Now

APPLY FOR THE CLAUDE CAMPUS AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

The programme materials also direct applicants to Anthropic’s campus page at anthropic.com/campus.

Is the Claude Campus Ambassador Program paid?

Yes. Selected ambassadors receive a USD 3,600 cash stipend.

Who can apply?

The programme has opportunities for undergraduates, graduate students, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers, with different tracks for each group.

What are the three programme tracks?

The three tracks are:

  1. Claude Builder Club – for undergraduate students
  2. Claude Campus Conversations – for graduate students
  3. Claude for Science – for PhD students and postdoctoral researchers

When is the application deadline?

Applications close September 12 at 11:59pm PT.

Where can I apply?

Applicants can apply through the programme’s application form.

Apply Now →

item.content:encoded:
The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) is inviting expressions of interest and nominations from suitably qualified individuals who may be considered for appointment to its Board of Directors. The opportunity provides individuals with an interest and experience in conservation, biodiversity protection, sustainable development and regional environmental governance with an opportunity to contribute to the strategic direction of an important Caribbean environmental fund.

The proposed Board appointment will run for a maximum of two years, with the proposed term beginning on 1 October 2026.

Applications and nominations must be submitted by 7 September 2026.

About the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund

The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) is a regional environmental fund established to provide stable, long-term financial resources for conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean.

The Fund plays a role in supporting long-term approaches to environmental conservation and sustainable development throughout the region. Its work involves the mobilization and management of financial resources intended to support biodiversity and ecosystem-related priorities.

As a regional institution handling resources for environmental and conservation purposes, effective governance and oversight are important to ensuring that the Fund operates responsibly and achieves meaningful strategic impact.

It is within this context that the CBF Governance Committee has opened a formal call for individuals who may be considered for vacant positions on its skills-based Board of Directors.

CBF Board of Directors Opportunity

The CBF is seeking expressions of interest and nominations from suitably qualified individuals for possible appointment to its Board of Directors.

The Board is described as skills-based, meaning that the selection process is intended to identify individuals whose knowledge, experience and professional capabilities can contribute to the governance and strategic oversight of the Fund.

The appointment is proposed for a maximum period of:

  • Two years
  • Proposed start date: 1 October 2026
  • Application deadline: 7 September 2026

The opportunity is therefore intended for individuals who are interested in contributing at a governance and strategic level to a regional organization focused on biodiversity conservation and environmental financing.

Why Serve on the CBF Board?

Serving on the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board provides an opportunity to contribute directly to the governance and strategic development of a regional institution working on biodiversity and conservation.

According to the opportunity announcement, Board members can contribute to several important areas.

1. Help Shape the Strategic Direction of the CBF

Directors will have an opportunity to contribute to the strategic direction of the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund.

Board-level participation can therefore involve contributing perspectives and expertise that help guide the institution’s priorities and long-term development.

The Board plays an important role in ensuring that the Fund continues to develop in a way that supports its conservation and biodiversity objectives.

2. Support Strong Governance

The CBF is seeking Board members as part of efforts to ensure:

  • Robust fiduciary oversight
  • Objective governance
  • Strategic impact

This makes Board participation particularly important because the Fund is responsible for managing resources intended to support environmental and conservation priorities.

Directors can contribute to the governance structures and oversight needed to support responsible institutional decision-making.

3. Contribute to Regional Conservation

The CBF’s work is focused on conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean.

Board members therefore have the opportunity to contribute to an institution whose activities are connected to some of the region’s broader environmental priorities.

The position provides an opportunity to support efforts aimed at protecting biodiversity and strengthening long-term financing for conservation.

4. Engage With Regional and International Partners

Board service can also provide opportunities for Directors to engage with partners working in conservation and sustainable development.

The announcement notes that Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF at:

  • Regional meetings
  • International meetings
  • Convenings
  • Other strategic engagements

Where appropriate, these engagements may also involve travel.

This can provide Board members with opportunities to participate in discussions involving Caribbean and international partners committed to conservation and sustainable development.

Nature of the Board Appointment

The CBF Board opportunity is different from a conventional employment position.

Board service is voluntary and does not carry remuneration.

This means individuals appointed to the Board should understand that they will not receive a salary or regular remuneration for their Board service.

However, Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF through regional and international engagements, including meetings and other strategic activities.

The announcement specifically notes that travel may be involved where appropriate.

Appointment Term

The proposed appointment is for a maximum of two years.

The proposed commencement date is:

1 October 2026

Applicants should therefore be prepared for the possibility of serving on the Board during the proposed two-year period, subject to the terms and conditions of the appointment.

Who Is This Opportunity For?

The CBF is specifically seeking suitably qualified individuals who may be considered for vacant positions on its skills-based Board of Directors.

The announcement emphasizes that the Board is skills-based, indicating that professional knowledge, expertise and relevant capabilities are important considerations.

However, the information provided in the announcement does not specify a detailed list of educational qualifications, years of professional experience, specific professional disciplines or individual technical skills required from applicants.

Therefore, applicants should carefully review the official application materials and nomination process for any additional requirements that may apply.

Geographic Eligibility

The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund is a regional Caribbean environmental fund, and the Board opportunity is connected to its work across the Caribbean.

However, the supplied announcement does not explicitly state a nationality restriction or provide a specific list of countries from which applicants must come.

It also does not provide a specific race or ethnicity requirement.

Applicants should therefore refer to the official CBF application materials for any additional geographic or eligibility requirements that may apply.

Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting an expression of interest or nomination is:

7 September 2026

Interested individuals should ensure that their applications or nominations are submitted before the stated deadline.

Because the opportunity is for Board-level service and the appointment is proposed to begin on 1 October 2026, interested candidates should allow sufficient time to review the requirements and prepare their submission.

APPLY HERE

Proposed Start Date

The proposed start date for the Board appointment is:

1 October 2026

The appointment is expected to run for a maximum of two years.

How to Apply

Individuals interested in being considered for the CBF Board of Directors should submit their expression of interest or nomination through the official application process.

Application deadline: 7 September 2026

Apply Now:
CBF Board of Directors Expression of Interest Application

Applicants should carefully review the official application form and provide the information requested as part of the expression-of-interest or nomination process.

Important Information for Potential Applicants

Before applying, candidates should understand several important aspects of the opportunity:

  1. It is a Board appointment opportunity, rather than a conventional employment vacancy.
  2. The appointment is proposed for a maximum of two years.
  3. The proposed start date is 1 October 2026.
  4. Board service is voluntary and unpaid.
  5. Directors may have opportunities to participate in regional and international meetings and strategic engagements.
  6. Travel may be involved where appropriate.
  7. The Board is described as skills-based.
  8. The CBF is seeking individuals who are suitably qualified to contribute to the governance and strategic direction of the Fund.
  9. The application deadline is 7 September 2026.
  10. The supplied announcement does not provide a detailed list of qualifications, professional experience requirements or nationality restrictions, so applicants should consult the official application materials for further information.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board of Directors 2026

About the CBF’s Governance Priorities

The call for Board members is closely connected to the CBF’s need for strong institutional governance.

The Fund was established to provide long-term financial resources for:

  • Conservation
  • Ecosystem-based adaptation
  • Biodiversity protection

Because these areas involve significant regional environmental priorities, the Board has an important role in supporting responsible governance and strategic decision-making.

The CBF Governance Committee is therefore seeking individuals who can potentially strengthen the Board’s collective skills and contribute to its fiduciary oversight, objective governance and strategic impact.

Conclusion

The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund Board of Directors Call for Expressions of Interest presents an opportunity for suitably qualified individuals to contribute to the governance and strategic direction of a regional institution dedicated to conservation, ecosystem-based adaptation and biodiversity protection across the Caribbean.

The proposed Board term is up to two years, beginning on 1 October 2026. Board service is voluntary and unpaid, although Directors may have opportunities to represent the CBF at regional and international meetings, convenings and other strategic engagements, including travel where appropriate.

Individuals interested in contributing at a governance level to Caribbean conservation and sustainable development should review the opportunity carefully and submit their expression of interest or nomination before the 7 September 2026 deadline.
